title: Opus host, gpt-5.6-sol delegates, 30 min caps, 3 h fences

roster.ruling: Delegates run codex gpt-5.6-sol. Ruled by the human 2026-08-09 before a 10-hour absence (recorded in metasystem/plans/unattended-run-20260809.md): two bm-2-shaped cohorts, host claude-opus-5 in both, delegates gpt-5.6-sol in this spec and devin swe-1-7 in bm-2, two repetitions each, same shape and fences as the completed bm-2 cohort. This spec exists as a sibling rather than an amendment for the same reason bm-2 does: a roster change is a new benchmark identity, and bm-1's cost ruling (luna, not sol) stays untouched — THIS spec's sol roster is the human's own instruction, not a revision of that ruling. Unlike swe-1-7, gpt-5.6-sol is paid: the fences bound spend exactly as they did for the completed bm-2 cohort.

fences.approved: hostTurnCapMin/jobCapMin revised 2026-08-11 by the human's role-caps ruling (implementers 25-30 minutes, host turn ~30 minutes, critics keep their configured cap-min), given via the in-session question component; the 2026-08-05 blanket approval covers the untouched fences; still an experiment per the promotion rule; ledgerNoGainBudget 8 set 2026-08-12 per the recorded last-defense sizing rule after cohort bm-2s-20260812t011219z-60201 repetition 1 parked at stop-loss on three honest scaffolding cycles

exposure.note: An estimate on the cheap roster (Opus host, gpt-5.6-luna delegates), revised down from EUR:75 when the human capped cost. No BM-1 run has happened, so this is a guess the first trial's recorded usage replaces; the fences stop the run long before the exposure does.

notes.roster: Pinned by exact model identifier when a run is prepared, never by a phrase like 'cheap models', because comparability requires two cohorts to share an identical roster. The identifier is gpt-5.6-sol, dispatched to the codex runtime.
notes.fences: Role-specific caps per the human's 2026-08-11 ruling: implementer dispatches carry --cap-min 25 to 30, critic dispatches keep their configured default; jobCapMin 30 is the circuit breaker bounding ANY job, sized to the largest ruled role cap rather than to Devin's inference profile (bm-2 v0.2 chose 180/240/12 for swe-1-7; sol jobs are minutes, not hours). wallClockHours stays 3: the v0.1 flat-floor cohorts died of a prompt-poisoning park, not the wall clock, and 30-minute jobs at concurrency 2 fit several full cycles. Caps protect against stuck loops; they do not define the experiment (the bm-2 v0.2 principle). ledgerNoGainBudget moved 3 to 8 (2026-08-12): repetition 1 of the first v0.2 cohort parked at stop-loss after exactly three unresolved cycles scoring self-assessment=0 — the count gate legitimately reads zero until package, tests, and the pinned test-command line all hold, so a budget of three measures the scaffolding phase, not the agent. The kit validator's own warning named this before launch. Eight equals the cycle fence: pure last defense, and ZERO marginal exposure because fence.cycles=8 already bounds total cycles — the resize cannot increase the approved spend ceiling.
